boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain United States Coast Guard Academy
boards.description: Ten food destinations in New London and nearby Groton with publicly posted late hours; confirm service availability before leaving campus.

cards.title: Denny's
cards.subtitle: 322 South Frontage Road, New London
cards.notes: Use the location page to check service options, then choose dine-in, pickup, or delivery for a meal at any hour.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 diner option in New London.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's lists this New London location as open 24/7 and offers dine-in, pickup, and delivery.
cards.source_title: Denny's — 322 South Frontage Road, New London
cards.access_notes: Posted store hours are 12:00 AM–11:58 PM every day; the page describes the location as 24/7.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Colman Street
cards.subtitle: 404 Colman Street, New London
cards.notes: Check the day-specific drive-through or dining-room schedule before heading out, especially when planning a very late pickup.
cards.short_summary: A Colman Street option with service into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-through service until 3 AM daily and until 4 AM Thursday through Saturday at this location.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 404 Colman St, New London
cards.access_notes: Drive-through posted until 3 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 4 AM Thursday–Saturday; dine-in hours are separately posted.

cards.title: Wendy's on Colman Street
cards.subtitle: 370 Colman Street, New London
cards.notes: Choose carryout, dining room, or drive-through service and verify the location page again if operating conditions change.
cards.short_summary: An all-week option posted until 3:30 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's lists restaurant and drive-through hours of 10 AM–3:30 AM every day for this New London location.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-through are both posted 10:00 AM–3:30 AM daily.

cards.title: McDonald's on Colman Street
cards.subtitle: 406 Colman Street, New London
cards.notes: Use the restaurant locator or app to confirm the active service mode before leaving, since lobby and drive-through hours can differ.
cards.short_summary: A Colman Street location listed through 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: The location listing for McDonald's at 406 Colman Street shows daily hours from 5 AM until 2 AM.
cards.access_notes: A current location listing reports 5:00 AM–2:00 AM daily; confirm service availability in the official locator before travel.

cards.title: Chili's New London
cards.subtitle: 369 North Frontage Road, New London
cards.notes: For a later sit-down meal or pickup, use the official location page and select a Friday or Saturday when midnight hours apply.
cards.short_summary: A family restaurant with midnight weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Chili's lists this New London restaurant open until midnight Friday and Saturday, and until 11 PM Sunday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: 11 AM–11 PM Sunday–Thursday and 11 AM–midnight Friday–Saturday; pickup and delivery are listed.

cards.title: Pizzarama Drive-In
cards.subtitle: 625 Broad Street, New London
cards.notes: Plan for a Friday or Saturday evening if you need the latest posted closing time, and check the restaurant site before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A Broad Street pizza stop open until 10 PM on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizzarama posts hours until 10 PM Friday and Saturday, with 9 PM closing the other days.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are 10:30 AM–10 PM Friday and Saturday, and 10:30 AM–9 PM Sunday through Thursday.

cards.title: Tony D's Italian Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 92 Huntington Street, New London
cards.notes: Reserve or call ahead for dinner, then use the posted Friday or Saturday schedule when planning a late meal downtown.
cards.short_summary: An Italian restaurant with 10 PM weekend closings.
cards.evidence_claim: Tony D's lists Friday and Saturday hours through 10 PM and identifies its New London address.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are 11:30 AM–10 PM Friday and Saturday; other listed dinner nights end at 9 PM.

cards.entity_name: Jasmine Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
cards.title: Jasmine Thai Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 470 Bank Street, New London
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s posted dinner schedule to time a takeout or dine-in visit; weekday lunch and dinner hours are separate.
cards.short_summary: Thai and sushi dining with 10 PM Friday and Saturday service.
cards.evidence_claim: Jasmine Thai posts dinner hours until 10 PM Friday and Saturday at 470 Bank Street.
cards.source_title: Jasmine Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
cards.access_notes: Dinner is posted until 10 PM Friday and Saturday, 9:30 PM Monday–Thursday and Sunday.

cards.title: Empire Pizza
cards.subtitle: 150 Broad Street, New London
cards.notes: Place a pickup or dine-in plan before the posted cutoff, using Friday or Saturday for the latest listed closing time.
cards.short_summary: A Broad Street pizza option listed until 9:45 PM on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Empire Pizza lists dine-in, pickup, and takeout at 150 Broad Street, with Friday and Saturday hours until 9:45 PM.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours end at 9:45 PM Friday and Saturday and 9:30 PM Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Sneekers Cafe
cards.subtitle: 568 Poquonnock Road, Groton
cards.notes: For a nearby off-campus dinner, check the cafe’s schedule and confirm seating or takeout details directly before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Groton cafe posted open until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Sneekers Cafe lists hours of 11 AM–midnight Tuesday through Sunday at its Groton location.
cards.access_notes: The official restaurant page posts Tuesday–Sunday hours of 11 AM–12 AM; confirm availability before travel.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Academy destinations where cadets study, train, gather, or take part in the shared campus program.

cards.title: Library at Waesche Hall
cards.subtitle: Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Bring a research task, a map-heavy assignment, or a group project; the library identifies quiet study, large tables, and collaborative spaces.
cards.short_summary: A flexible academic workspace with quiet and collaborative options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy Library in Waesche Hall provides large tables, collaborative spaces for group projects, and quiet study space.
cards.source_title: Library — United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: Library services are for cadets, faculty, and staff; verify visitor access with the Academy before arrival.

cards.title: Hewitt Writing and Reading Center
cards.subtitle: Second deck of the Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Schedule a session or upload work through the center’s scheduling program when you want feedback from mentors, tutors, writers, or educators.
cards.short_summary: Writing and reading support located inside the Academy Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hewitt Writing and Reading Center is on the second deck of the Library in Waesche Hall and provides mentoring and tutoring to cadets in every class year and major.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources — United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: The catalog says cadets can make appointments through the online scheduling program.

cards.title: Chase Hall
cards.subtitle: Cadet barracks and All Hands Dining Facility
cards.notes: Use the building as a landmark for core cadet life: the campus map identifies both cadet barracks and the All Hands Dining Facility here.
cards.short_summary: A central cadet-life building that combines housing and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy campus map lists Chase Hall as the location of the All Hands Dining Facility, cadet barracks, and Cadet Store.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: On-campus dining is available to faculty, staff, cadets with some limitations, and visitors; Academy security rules apply.

cards.title: Leamy Hall
cards.subtitle: Auditorium, bowling alley, cafés, and Coast Guard Band
cards.notes: Check the Academy calendar for a band concert or event, and use the map-listed cafés and bowling alley as on-campus gathering points.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use campus building with performance, recreation, and café spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy campus map identifies Leamy Hall as containing an auditorium, bowling alley, cafés, MWR office, chaplains, and the U.S. Coast Guard Band.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Public attendance at Coast Guard Band concerts is subject to the Academy’s security posture.

cards.title: Roland Hall Gym
cards.subtitle: Athletics facilities
cards.notes: Look for Academy athletics programming around this map-listed gym; physical development and sports are part of the cadet program.
cards.short_summary: A named campus gym within the Academy’s broad athletics program.
cards.evidence_claim: Roland Hall Gym is identified on the Academy campus map, and the Academy states that every cadet competes through varsity, club, or intramural sports.
cards.source_title: Athletics — United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: Use the Academy campus map to locate Roland Hall Gym; access may be limited by Academy operations.

cards.title: Cadet Memorial Field
cards.subtitle: Athletics field
cards.notes: Watch for an Academy athletic event or use the field as a clear campus waypoint; varsity, club, and intramural participation involves every cadet.
cards.short_summary: A named Academy athletics field tied to the cadet sports program.
cards.evidence_claim: Cadet Memorial Field is identified on the Academy campus map, and the Academy says every cadet participates in varsity, club, or intramural sports.
cards.source_title: Athletics — United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: Event and spectator access depend on the Academy schedule and security posture.

cards.title: Sailing Center
cards.subtitle: Academy waterfront
cards.notes: Spot the waterfront training infrastructure from an approved campus route and consult Academy programming before expecting access to boats or instruction.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed waterfront destination supporting the Academy’s maritime setting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy campus map identifies a Sailing Center and Sail Loft on the waterfront side of campus.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Waterfront facilities may be operational or restricted; remain on permitted visitor routes.

cards.title: Rowing Center
cards.subtitle: Academy waterfront
cards.notes: Use this named waterfront destination to orient a campus walk, then check the athletics schedule for any public-facing rowing activity.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed rowing facility on the Academy waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy campus map identifies the Rowing Center as a named campus destination.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Access to training areas and waterfront operations may be restricted.

cards.title: Barque Eagle
cards.subtitle: Academy waterfront
cards.notes: When the vessel is in port and viewable from an approved route, use it as a tangible link to cadet sail training and Academy maritime history.
cards.short_summary: The Coast Guard’s tall ship and a cadet training vessel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy identifies the 295-foot Barque EAGLE as the Coast Guard flagship and a training vessel for Coast Guard Academy cadets.
cards.source_title: Tenants — United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: The vessel’s presence and boarding access vary with its operational schedule; do not expect public access without confirmation.

cards.title: Bear Plaza
cards.subtitle: Campus mascot memorial
cards.notes: Pause at the plaza’s Objee statue and connect it to a documented piece of Academy identity before heading to an athletic event or pep rally.
cards.short_summary: The campus location that memorializes the Academy’s bear mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy history page states that Objee is memorialized by a statue in Bear Plaza and that the mascot appears at pep rallies and athletic events.
cards.source_title: History — United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: Follow Academy visitor and security requirements while on campus.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase outings in New London or nearby, each supported by a current direct-access source.

cards.title: Walk the Native Plant Collection
cards.subtitle: Connecticut College Arboretum, New London
cards.notes: Enter through the Williams Street entrance and take a self-guided walk among the collection’s labeled native plants; stay on paths and follow Arboretum policies.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided native-plant walk on an Arboretum collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College states that Arboretum general admission is free to the public and identifies the Native Plant Collection entrance on Williams Street.
cards.source_title: Hours and Policies | Connecticut College Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily from sunrise to sunset; general admission is free. Follow posted Arboretum rules.

cards.title: Pause in the Caroline Black Garden
cards.subtitle: Connecticut College Arboretum, New London
cards.notes: Use the Mohegan Avenue/Route 32 entrance to explore the named garden at your own pace; bring only what you need and leave plants undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A named garden stop within the public Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College lists the Caroline Black Garden among Arboretum access points and states general Arboretum admission is free to the public.
cards.source_title: Hours and Policies | Connecticut College Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily from sunrise to sunset; general admission is free. Follow posted Arboretum rules.

cards.title: Make a tree-spotting loop
cards.subtitle: Campus Tree Collection, Connecticut College, New London
cards.notes: Start from the college’s main entrance and use the campus setting for a low-key tree-spotting loop; respect active campus operations and posted access rules.
cards.short_summary: A campus collection suited to a no-cost outdoor stroll.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College offers free, public Campus Tree Collection guided tours and states Arboretum general admission is free to the public.
cards.access_notes: The program page lists free Campus Tree Collection tours open to the public without preregistration; verify individual tour dates before going.

cards.title: Take an easy jogging-trail lap
cards.subtitle: Connecticut College Arboretum, New London
cards.notes: Use only the designated jogging trails between Route 32 and the Thames River, or paved campus roads, and keep the outing gentle and trail-friendly.
cards.short_summary: A designated, no-cost route for a run or walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College states that general Arboretum admission is free to the public and permits jogging only on its designated jogging trails or paved campus roads.
cards.source_title: Hours and Policies | Connecticut College Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily from sunrise to sunset; remain on designated jogging routes and follow Arboretum policies.

cards.title: Follow the self-guided Arboretum tour
cards.subtitle: Connecticut College Arboretum, New London
cards.notes: Pick up the self-guided brochure at a listed entrance, then move slowly through the grounds with friends while observing the Arboretum’s ecology rules.
cards.short_summary: A brochure-led outdoor activity with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College says self-guided tour brochures are available at Arboretum entrances and that general admission is free to the public.
cards.source_title: Hours and Policies | Connecticut College Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily from sunrise to sunset; brochures are listed at Native Plant Collection, North Entrance, and Caroline Black Garden access points.

cards.title: Cheer at a Connecticut College game
cards.subtitle: Connecticut College, New London
cards.notes: Check the athletics calendar, choose a scheduled varsity contest, and bring a friend to watch from the stands without buying a ticket.
cards.short_summary: A calendar-based, no-ticket campus sports outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College states that admission is free to all sporting events and directs visitors to its athletics calendar for upcoming games.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free to all sporting events; consult the athletics calendar for dates, locations, and any event-specific changes.

cards.title: Browse the Lyman Allyn galleries
cards.subtitle: 625 Williams Street, New London
cards.notes: Bring your USCGA student identification and spend time with the museum’s galleries; confirm the day’s hours before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: USCGA students have free museum admission with the applicable status.
cards.evidence_claim: Lyman Allyn Art Museum lists students and staff at USCGA among groups receiving free admission.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission | Lyman Allyn Art Museum
cards.access_notes: USCGA students and staff are listed as free; the museum lists Tuesday–Saturday and Sunday visiting hours, with last entry at 4 p.m.

cards.title: Walk the waterfront promenade
cards.subtitle: Waterfront Park, New London
cards.notes: Meet at City Pier and walk the improved half-mile promenade, stopping for river views and public art while respecting any event-area restrictions.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront walk with a documented no-fee access point.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut DEEP describes City Pier and Waterfront Park as having an improved half-mile promenade, public art displays, and no parking fee.
cards.source_title: Connecticut Coastal Access Guide: City Pier and Waterfront Park
cards.access_notes: DEEP lists on-street parking with no fee. Major events may impose access rules; the city prohibits alcohol containers on city-owned property.

cards.title: Trace the paths at Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: Memorial Park, New London
cards.notes: Use the park’s walking paths for a short outdoor catch-up, noticing the lawn, terrace, and grades described in its historic landscape design.
cards.short_summary: A public city park designed around connected walking paths.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies Memorial Park in New London as city-managed and describes its walking paths, upper lawn, and terrace design.
cards.access_notes: City-managed outdoor park; use the paths responsibly and observe any posted municipal rules.

cards.title: Walk to Fort Trumbull State Park
cards.subtitle: 90 Walbach Street, New London
cards.notes: Approach on foot and explore the state-park grounds with a friend; this keeps the outing centered on the free park admission rather than paid historic-building entry.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian-accessible state-park grounds walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut DEEP states that Fort Trumbull State Park admission is free when arriving by bus and provides a walking route from New London Union Station.
cards.source_title: Fort Trumbull State Park ParkConneCT Guide
cards.access_notes: DEEP’s guide gives a one-mile walking route from New London Union Station and says park admission is free when arriving by bus. Historic-building admission may differ.

warnings: Confirm individual venue schedules and any event-specific closures before visiting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct study settings in the Library at Waesche Hall, selected for their documented individual, group, research, or writing-support affordances.

cards.title: Library Large Tables
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Bring charts, readings, or a project with room to spread out; the Academy specifically identifies these tables as a Library study option.
cards.short_summary: A documented Library option for work that needs a broad tabletop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy lists large tables among Library spaces for individual and group learning.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources | United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: The Library is in Waesche Hall and serves Academy cadets, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Library Collaboration Workstations
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Use this documented collaboration setting when a project calls for working alongside classmates; confirm current availability with Library staff.
cards.short_summary: A Library setting identified for collaborative learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy lists collaboration workstations among Library spaces for individual and group learning.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources | United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: Check with Library staff for current availability or any use procedures.

cards.title: Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Choose a documented study room for a contained session, then ask Library staff about current access or any reservation procedure.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed Library spaces listed for individual and group learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy identifies study rooms as Library spaces available for individual and group learning.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources | United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: Current room availability and any reservation rules should be confirmed with the Library.

cards.title: Library Small Group Tables
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Set up a small working session at the Library’s documented group tables; use them for shared notes, problem sets, or peer review.
cards.short_summary: A table-based setting for small-group academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy lists small group tables among Library spaces for individual and group learning.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources | United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: Library space is provided for Academy cadets, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Library Individual Carrels
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Use an individual carrel for a quiet reading or writing block; the Academy expressly identifies these carrels for quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet-study option inside the Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy lists individual carrels for quiet study in the Library.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources | United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: The Library is located in Waesche Hall.

cards.title: Hewitt Writing and Reading Center
cards.subtitle: Second deck of the Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Make an appointment and bring a draft or reading assignment; HWRC mentors and tutors assist cadets across class years and majors.
cards.short_summary: A staffed writing and reading support center within the Library.
cards.evidence_claim: HWRC is on the Library’s second deck and provides mentors and tutors for cadets in all class years and majors.
cards.source_title: Cadet Life and Resources | United States Coast Guard Academy Catalog
cards.access_notes: Cadets can make appointments through an online scheduling program; the catalog lists Sunday–Thursday evenings and most business hours.

cards.title: Library Research Assistance
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Bring a research question to Library staff for help locating, evaluating, organizing, or citing authoritative sources for an assignment.
cards.short_summary: A staffed starting point for research-intensive coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Library staff assist with research, locating resources, organizing and citing sources, credibility analysis, and literature reviews.
cards.source_title: Library - United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: The Academy says the Library serves cadets, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Library Quiet Study Space
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Choose the Library when you need a quiet work setting, then use its carrels or another available quiet-study area for focused reading.
cards.short_summary: A Library environment expressly described as supporting quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy describes the Library as offering quiet study space as well as collaboration and large-table options.
cards.source_title: Library - United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: Ask Library staff to help identify the available quiet-study setting.

cards.title: Library Comfortable Chairs
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Settle into the Library’s comfortable chairs for an evening reading or review block after confirming that the space is available.
cards.short_summary: A seated Library study setting described in the Academy’s cadet-life guide.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy’s cadet-life guide says cadets may choose the Library and its comfortable chairs during evening study time.
cards.source_title: A Day in the Life - United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: This page describes a 7:00 p.m. evening study period; it does not state Library operating hours.

cards.title: Library Coffee and Tea Seating
cards.subtitle: Library, Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Pair a reading session with the Library’s documented coffee and tea offering, while following any current Academy or Library guidance.
cards.short_summary: A Library study setting associated with a documented coffee-and-tea offering.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy’s cadet-life guide says the Library has comfortable chairs and free coffee and tea.
cards.source_title: A Day in the Life - United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.access_notes: The source describes this in the context of evening study; verify current availability locally.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named downtown New London destinations along documented corridors near the Academy.

cards.title: Hygienic Art on Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Walk Bank Street to 79–83 and check the gallery’s current exhibition or Art Park program before planning a visit.
cards.short_summary: A documented gallery and art-park stop on the downtown Bank Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut’s tourism office lists Hygienic Art Galleries & Art Park at 79–83 Bank Street and describes it as a venue for emerging and established artists.
cards.access_notes: The source lists gallery hours; confirm the current exhibition and access details directly before going.

cards.title: Custom House on Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Use Bank Street to reach 150 Bank Street and focus your visit on the museum’s New London waterfront collections.
cards.short_summary: A maritime-history destination on the same downtown corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the New London Customhouse at 150 Bank Street as a National Register site managed by the New London Maritime Society.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and visiting arrangements may apply; check the operator’s current information.

cards.title: Garde on State Street
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Head to 325 State Street and review the current calendar for performances, films, or education programs.
cards.short_summary: A named performing-arts venue on State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Garde Arts Center’s official site gives its address as 325 State Street, New London.
cards.access_notes: Ticketing and event availability vary; consult the center’s current schedule.

cards.entity_name: Timothy Green’s New London Summary Site
cards.title: Timothy Green’s State Street site
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Pause at 158 State Street and use the city’s historic-figures page to connect the building with early Connecticut newspapers.
cards.short_summary: A surviving 1771 State Street building tied to New London’s early press history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London identifies 158 State Street as the site of Timothy Green’s New London Summary and says the 1771 building survived the burning of the city.
cards.access_notes: View from the public street; the source documents the historic site but does not state public interior access.

cards.title: Hotel Bristol on Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Find the 90 Bank Street trail location and read the city’s Black Heritage Trail entry before or while you walk the block.
cards.short_summary: A Bank Street stop included in New London’s Black Heritage Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London’s Black Heritage Trail lists the Hotel Bristol at 90 Bank Street and documents its connection to a 1919 racial-violence incident.
cards.access_notes: This is a historic trail location; use public sidewalks and respect any private property.

cards.title: Shiloh on Garvin Street
cards.subtitle: Garvin Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Include 1 Garvin Street on a heritage walk and use the city’s trail entry for context on the congregation’s history.
cards.short_summary: New London’s oldest historically Black church, documented by the city trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London lists Shiloh Baptist Church at 1 Garvin Street and identifies it as the city’s oldest historically Black church.
cards.access_notes: Observe from public areas unless the church publicly invites visitors inside.

cards.title: Amistad Pier at Waterfront Park
cards.subtitle: Water Street waterfront corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Use the waterfront path to locate the Amistad Pier entrance and read the trail account of the schooner’s 1839 arrival.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront trail stop interpreting New London’s connection to La Amistad.
cards.evidence_claim: New London’s Black Heritage Trail identifies the Amistad Pier entrance at Waterfront Park and recounts that the schooner was towed into New London Harbor in 1839.
cards.access_notes: Use the public waterfront park entrance; the source does not list an admission charge.

cards.title: 38 Green Street’s civic-history stop
cards.subtitle: Green Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Add 38 Green Street to a self-guided heritage walk and use the city trail page for the site’s civic-history context.
cards.short_summary: A Green Street Black Heritage Trail location tied to community organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: The city’s Black Heritage Trail says 38 Green Street housed the New England Peoples Finance Corporation and United Negro Welfare Council in the late 1920s.
cards.access_notes: View from the public right-of-way and respect the property’s current use.

cards.title: Antone DeSant’s Bank Street site
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Locate 745 Bank Street and read the city’s entry on DeSant and the Cape Verdean whalers who came to New England.
cards.short_summary: A named Bank Street site on the Black Heritage Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London’s Black Heritage Trail lists the Antone DeSant site at 745 Bank Street and describes DeSant’s arrival as part of a wave of Cabo Verdeans on whaling vessels.
cards.access_notes: This is a historic-location stop; view it from public areas unless access is explicitly offered.

cards.title: Spark on Union Street
cards.subtitle: Union Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Walk to 7 Union Street and check Spark Maker Space’s current public program or workshop details before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A named creative-workspace destination on Union Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London’s Explore New London site states that Spark Maker Space moved to 7 Union Street in downtown New London.
cards.source_title: New London Tales – Explore New London
cards.access_notes: Workshop access and costs vary by program; verify current visitor information with Spark Maker Space.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Coast Guard Academy customs, ceremonies, and objects that mark cadet life from Swab Summer through commissioning.

cards.title: 100th Day role reversal
cards.subtitle: Fourth Class Cadets take the lead for a day
cards.notes: Look for Academy coverage around 100 days before graduation; the custom briefly reverses parts of the fourth- and second-class routine.
cards.short_summary: A calendar-marked reversal of cadet hierarchy.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says that, typically 100 days before graduation, Fourth Class Cadets become “kings for a day” while Second Class Cadets obey their commands.
cards.access_notes: A cadet tradition; confirm any public observation options with the Academy calendar.

cards.title: The class ring arrives in April
cards.subtitle: A signet ring with Academy and class crests
cards.notes: Notice the Academy crest and individual class crest on the signet ring, then connect it to the later Ring Dance christening.
cards.short_summary: A wearable cadet symbol that stays with alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that Second Class Cadets receive the signet ring in April; it bears the Academy crest and the individual’s class crest.
cards.access_notes: A personal cadet item; view only when displayed publicly or by invitation.

cards.title: A photo tucked into the cover
cards.subtitle: Cadets personalize the inside of a uniform hat
cards.notes: If a cadet chooses to show you their cover, ask about the photo inside; the Academy identifies this as a tradition for loved ones.
cards.short_summary: A private personal detail inside a formal uniform item.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says it is tradition for cadets to place a picture of a loved one or someone special in their combination cover.
cards.access_notes: Personal uniform item; do not handle or photograph without the owner’s permission.

cards.title: Two silver dollars at commissioning
cards.subtitle: One for the Anchor Cadet and one for a first salute
cards.notes: Watch commencement coverage for the silver-dollar custom and the moment loved ones commonly place new ensigns’ shoulder boards.
cards.short_summary: A commissioning ritual built around two pocketed coins.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says graduating ensigns carry two silver dollars: one for the Anchor Cadet and one for the first person to render a salute.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during commencement; follow Academy visitor guidance for attendance.

cards.title: The Chase Hall words no one steps on
cards.subtitle: “Who Lives Here Reveres Honor, Honors Duty”
cards.notes: Find the inlaid Quarterdeck words in Chase Hall and observe the custom respectfully; do not step on the inscription.
cards.short_summary: An inlaid phrase treated as a physical symbol of the Honor Concept.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy identifies the words inlaid on the Quarterdeck of Chase Hall as a symbol of honor and says they should never be tread upon.
cards.access_notes: Chase Hall access may be restricted; follow posted access rules and Academy instructions.

cards.title: Ring the black buoy for luck
cards.subtitle: The navigational buoy by the museum
cards.notes: Locate the black navigational buoy by the museum and treat it gently; Academy tradition associates ringing it with good luck.
cards.short_summary: A buoy turned into a campus luck ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that tradition holds a cadet who rings the black navigational buoy by the museum will be granted good luck.
cards.access_notes: Confirm campus and museum-area access before visiting; respect the object and surrounding grounds.

cards.title: Dress the bear before game day
cards.subtitle: The Academy mascot stands behind Chase Hall
cards.notes: See whether Objee is dressed for an upcoming game or event, and photograph the statue only from publicly accessible grounds.
cards.short_summary: A black-bear mascot statue that changes outfits for campus spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says Objee is its black-bear mascot and that the statue behind Chase Hall is commonly dressed up for major events and athletic games.
cards.access_notes: Located in the park behind Chase Hall; comply with campus visitor and photography rules.

cards.title: Christen a class ring with seven oceans
cards.subtitle: A Saturday-before-graduation rite at the Ring Monument
cards.notes: Follow official Graduation Week information for this formal event; the ring’s seven-oceans christening is the central documented ritual.
cards.short_summary: A formal transition toward first-class year.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says that at Ring Dance, each couple proceeds to the Ring Monument and the escort dips the ring into water from the world’s seven oceans.
cards.access_notes: Held during Graduation Week; attendance and access are determined by Academy event guidance.

cards.title: The end of being a Swab
cards.subtitle: Upper-class cadets pin on Fourth Class shoulder boards
cards.notes: Watch for the Crown Park ceremony before classes begin, when former Swabs formally enter the Corps of Cadets.
cards.short_summary: A visible handoff from Swab Summer to cadet status.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that, at the end of Swab Summer, upper-class cadets affix Fourth Class shoulder boards on former Swabs in a Crown Park ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Occurs before classes start; check Academy communications for any visitor arrangements.

cards.title: Find out the first Coast Guard assignment
cards.subtitle: First Class Cadets learn their initial billets together
cards.notes: Look for official Billet Night coverage to see the annual reveal, when graduating cadets learn their first Coast Guard assignments.
cards.short_summary: An annual career-reveal ceremony for the senior class.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy describes Billet Night as an annual tradition in which First Class Cadets learn where they will go for their first Coast Guard assignment.
cards.access_notes: An Academy event; public attendance is not stated on the cited page.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at United States Coast Guard Academy, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that starts with campus orientation, moves through its waterfront and shared spaces, and ends with a scheduled Academy activity.

cards.entity_name: United States Coast Guard Academy Self-Guided Tour
cards.title: Start with a self-guided campus walk
cards.subtitle: Arrival and orientation · United States Coast Guard Academy
cards.notes: Download the official campus map, wear walking shoes, and use the route to orient yourself to the Academy’s hills, waterfront, and major buildings.
cards.short_summary: Get the lay of the land before choosing a place to linger.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy encourages visitors to take a self-guided tour and provides a campus map; it notes that the waterfront campus has hills.
cards.access_notes: Academy access is subject to its security posture; adults should bring valid photo identification and vehicles/occupants may be searched.

cards.title: Find Bear Plaza on the map
cards.subtitle: Early walk stop · campus landmark
cards.notes: Use this named plaza as a map-reading checkpoint, then identify the nearby academic, athletic, and waterfront destinations before continuing your walk.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark for getting oriented.
cards.evidence_claim: Bear Plaza is listed as a numbered destination on the Academy’s official campus map.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Follow current Academy access and security requirements.

cards.title: Visit the Coast Guard Museum when open
cards.subtitle: History stop · Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Check whether museum access is available during your visit, then use the historical artifacts to connect the Academy setting with Coast Guard service history.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum with Coast Guard historical artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy identifies the Coast Guard Museum as being on campus and says it contains an extensive collection of historical artifacts.
cards.access_notes: Confirm museum availability before going; Academy access is subject to security requirements.

cards.entity_name: United States Coast Guard Academy Library
cards.title: Set aside a quiet library block
cards.subtitle: Study reset · Waesche Hall
cards.notes: Bring a project, reading, or research question and choose a quiet or collaborative space; library staff can help locate authoritative sources.
cards.short_summary: A study stop with quiet and collaborative spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy Library in Waesche Hall offers quiet study space, collaborative spaces, research resources, and staff assistance.
cards.access_notes: Library services are described for Academy cadets, faculty, and staff; verify visitor access if you are not part of the Academy community.

cards.title: Pause at the Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Reflective stop · highest point in New London
cards.notes: Walk by the nondenominational chapel and, if a program is open to you, check the current schedule rather than assuming a service is underway.
cards.short_summary: A landmark chapel supporting Academy religious life.
cards.evidence_claim: The Coast Guard Memorial Chapel is the center of religious life at the Academy and hosts a variety of weekly services and programs.
cards.access_notes: Programs and access may vary; follow current Academy entry requirements.

cards.title: Continue to the Sailing Center waterfront
cards.subtitle: Waterfront walk · Academy campus
cards.notes: Use the map to reach the named Sailing Center and take in the waterfront setting from permitted areas; do not enter docks or facilities without authorization.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed waterfront destination on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sailing Center is a numbered destination on the Academy’s official campus map, and the Academy describes its campus as a waterfront facility.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Stay in authorized public areas and follow current Academy security instructions.

cards.title: Spot USCGC RAZORBILL from the waterfront
cards.subtitle: Maritime landmark · Academy waterfront
cards.notes: Locate this named cutter on the official map and view it only from authorized areas; treat it as an operational Coast Guard asset, not a boarding opportunity.
cards.short_summary: A named cutter shown on the Academy campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: USCGC RAZORBILL is listed as a numbered destination on the Academy’s official campus map.
cards.source_title: United States Coast Guard Academy Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Viewing and access depend on Academy security rules; do not attempt to board.

cards.title: Check the schedule for an athletic event
cards.subtitle: Afternoon option · Cadet Memorial Field
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled Bears event and attend only if it is open under current Academy procedures; otherwise use the field as a map stop on your walk.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic field and possible event setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Cadet Memorial Field is listed on the official campus map, and the Academy says the public may attend athletic events subject to its security posture.
cards.access_notes: Check the event schedule and Academy access conditions before attending.

cards.title: Look for a regimental review
cards.subtitle: Ceremonial stop · Washington Parade Field
cards.notes: Check the Academy calendar before planning around a review, then observe from authorized areas and give marching formations the right of way.
cards.short_summary: A named parade field for scheduled regimental activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Washington Parade Field is listed on the official campus map, and the Academy welcomes the public to Regimental Reviews subject to its security posture.
cards.access_notes: Regimental Reviews are scheduled events; visitors must follow Academy security instructions and yield to marching formations.

cards.title: End with a cadet music or drama performance
cards.subtitle: Evening option · check the current performance schedule
cards.notes: If a public performance is scheduled, reserve or confirm entry through the Academy’s current information; choose the production rather than assuming a nightly show.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled arts option produced with cadet participation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy describes an annual professionally produced cadet musical that is embraced by the Academy community and the public.
cards.access_notes: Performance dates, venue, admission, and public availability must be confirmed for the current season.
